note: Control titles are short paraphrases. Verify IDs and copy exact wording from the official NIST CSF 2.0 document before submitting. CSF 1.1 PR.AC-x was replaced by PR.AA-x in CSF 2.0; ISO 27001:2013 A.9 became A.5.15-A.5.18 / A.8.x in the 2022 revision.

multi_stage_extra_controls.title: Information on adverse events is correlated from multiple sources
Incidents are declared when events meet defined incident criteria

brute_force.title: Brute-force authentication attempts

nist_csf_2_0.title: Users, services and hardware are authenticated
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored

remediation: Block or rate-limit the offending source IP at the firewall/WAF
Enforce account lockout or progressive delays and require MFA on the targeted service
Alert on N failed logins per source/account per window
Reset credentials of any account that received a successful login after the failures

login_success.title: Successful login after repeated failures (possible account compromise)

nist_csf_2_0.title: Users, services and hardware are authenticated
Access permissions are managed with least privilege and separation of duties
Potentially adverse events are analysed to understand associated activity

remediation: Immediately disable the account, revoke active sessions/tokens and force a password reset
Review everything the account did after the login (commands, files, new accounts)
Enforce MFA and restrict the service to trusted source networks

port_scan.title: Network port scanning / reconnaissance

nist_csf_2_0.title: Networks and network services are monitored for adverse events
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorised logical access

remediation: Block the scanning source and review firewall rules to expose only required ports
Add IDS/IPS or rate-based rules for sequential multi-port probing
Confirm whether the source is an authorised scanner; if so, allow-list it explicitly

c2_beaconing.title: Periodic outbound connections consistent with C2 beaconing

nist_csf_2_0.title: Networks and network services are monitored for adverse events
Potentially adverse events are analysed to understand associated activity
Threat intelligence and context are integrated into analysis

remediation: Isolate the host and run EDR/malware triage
Block the destination IP/domain at the proxy or firewall and check threat-intel reputation
Hunt for the same destination across other hosts
Confirm the traffic is not a legitimate monitoring/update agent before blocking

exfiltration.title: Large outbound data transfer to an external destination (possible exfiltration)

nist_csf_2_0.title: Data in transit is protected (confidentiality, integrity, availability)
Networks and network services are monitored for adverse events
Potentially adverse events are analysed to understand associated activity

remediation: Block egress to the destination and isolate the source system
Identify what data was transferred and assess breach-notification obligations
Apply egress filtering and DLP rules for large transfers from database/file servers
Rotate credentials used on the affected system

priv_escalation.title: Suspicious administrative activity (possible privilege escalation)

nist_csf_2_0.title: Access permissions are managed with least privilege and separation of duties
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored

remediation: Verify with the account owner; disable the account if the activity is not legitimate
Remove unnecessary admin rights and require just-in-time privileged access
Alert on admin actions by non-admin accounts or outside change windows

anomalous_activity.title: Unclassified anomalous activity flagged by the model

nist_csf_2_0.title: Potentially adverse events are analysed to understand associated activity

remediation: Triage manually: review the raw events and surrounding context
Feed the analyst verdict back as a label for the next model retraining
